subject: Post-call recap: request/response data hygiene & residency constraints (BrightPath)
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@brightpath.health>, Emily Turner <emily.turner@brightpath.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: request/response data hygiene & residency constraints (BrightPath)

Hi Sanjay / Emily — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of your top priorities:
- Ensure any PII in request/response logs is either redacted or pseudonymized before leaving BrightPath’s VPC.
- Retain only minimal request metadata for 30 days for debugging; full payloads must be tenant-controlled and/or never persist beyond 48 hours unless explicitly allowed.
- Trace IDs and certain headers (Bayes-Trace, user_cookie_id) need to be suppressed or hashed in exported audit streams.
- Data residency: production inference in us-east1; audit exports should remain inside BrightPath’s project or be pushed to an s3 bucket in us-east-1 under your control.

Proposed short-term plan (we offered on the call):
1) Technical options doc: outline three approaches (inline redaction at edge, post-ingest scrub, prefix-KV caching w/never-persist policy). We’ll attach a draft playbook. (SEE ATTACHMENT: redaction_playbook_v1.pdf)
2) Pilot: sample 72-hour stream with obfuscated headers and nullified payload retention to validate latency & cost impact.
3) Compliance checkpoint: provide SOC2-relevant logs (access audit only) and sample sanitized event sets for review.

Could you confirm:
- Is 30 days the upper bound you want for minimal metadata?
- Any headers beyond the ones we discussed that require special handling?

Next steps: if you confirm, we’ll schedule a technical pilot kickoff next week and share the playbook + data-flow diagram. Monica will own the pilot coordination / procurement prep.

Thanks — Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0126
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: request/response data hygiene & residency constraints (BrightPath)

Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Retention: 30 days for minimal metadata is fine as an initial bound, but security wants an option for 7-day rolling retention on anything that contains even hashed identifiers. Can you show cost delta for 7d vs 30d in the pilot?

2) Headers: add X-Forwarded-For and any session cookie headers to the suppression list. We also use a vendor header X-BPH-Trace that we’d prefer to map-to-pseudonym rather than drop — helps debugging.

3) Residency: we require that any archive exports are stored in our AWS account (us-east-1) — not on Redwood-managed buckets. Is that supported for the pilot?

Also, procurement asked if we can get a redlineable SOW and a rough estimate for Dedicated capacity if the pilot validates. Emily will loop procurement.

— Sanjay

- Implement suppression for X-Forwarded-For and session cookie headers; pseudonymization for X-BPH-Trace.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Post-call recap: request/response data hygiene & residency constraints (BrightPath)

Sofia / team — quick technical readout: 

- Pseudonymization: we can support a deterministic hash (HMAC with customer salt) on X-BPH-Trace at the ingress proxy layer without touching the model payload path. That means trace correlation within BrightPath’s environment still works if they share the salt. No runtime change required for basic hashing; we already support header transforms in the edge config.

- Suppression: X-Forwarded-For and session cookies can be dropped at the edge. We’ll add a suppression rule in the pilot config.

- Retention: minimal metadata retention (request ID, timestamp, route, model version, latency) can be configured per-route. We’ll instrument the pilot to emit two retention buckets (7d and 30d) so we can compare ingestion volume and storage cost. Note: 7d retention reduces storage but will increase debugging friction for intermittent issues.

- Export to customer S3: supported via cross-account role; we need BrightPath to create an IAM role with a trust policy for our export principal and share the ARN. We’ll provide a template CloudFormation for them.

ETA: pilot config + playbook update (inc. retention table) — 3 business days after we get the sample log schema and an S3 role ARN. Instrumentation to collect cost delta — additional 2 business days. Total: ~5 business days.

I’m attaching a quick retention options table (retention_options_table.xlsx) and a draft edge transform snippet.

— Dev

All — sounds feasible. Proposed pilot timeline (high-level):
- Day 0: Kickoff with BrightPath(45m) to validate sample schema and confirm S3 ARN.
- Day 1–2: Provision pilot edge config, enable suppression/pseudonymize rules, deliver updated playbook.
- Day 3–5: Run 72-hour live stream; collect metrics (ingest volume, per-token latency, cost delta for 7d vs 30d).
- Day 6: Deliver pilot report and recommend next steps (pilot->Dedicated path + SOW).

I’ll book the kickoff for Monday 09:00 PT if that works for them. Monica — can you own procurement touchpoints and gather the S3 role? Also prep a light SOW template we can send as a draft.

— Dylan
